notes.body: Bōya is a fond way to call a little child, usually a boy. Here both parents use it for their baby girl.
Umma-umma is baby talk for food, something like yum-yum, cried out with delight.
The same bare word opened the story. Heard at last after the room has gone quiet, it closes the evening without comment.

data.say: Kept Casual to Bōya and umma-umma and held the storm-frame note for Curious, with nothing the context already gives.
